criteria.describe: A teammate skimming on a phone learns what changed and whether it touches their work.
Someone who joined last week gets the plain idea without internal jargon.
Someone building on the project sees what changed in what they use, and what's coming.
Every chart, number and caption says what the data and the picture support, no more.
In the pictures, text is big enough and sparse enough to read on a phone, and nothing crowds or collides.
The first short gives the story's point on its own; each one after it adds something; nothing repeats another thread.
As few shorts and words as the story allows: every short is one a teammate would miss if it were cut, and each reads in its seconds.

thread.title: Failed webhooks now retry on their own

cards.headline: Retries show in the event log

shorts.headline: Webhook delivery gets exponential backoff with jitter
shorts.caption: On a 5xx or timeout the dispatcher re-enqueues the event with backoff from 250 ms, doubling to 6 h, plus ±20% jitter, keyed by an idempotency key so receivers can dedupe.
shorts.why: Transient receiver outages no longer drop events.
shorts.picture: nine attempts on a log-scale axis, each with its delay in ms; small labels overlap near the start

shorts.headline: Retries live in the dispatch_queue table
shorts.caption: A new next_attempt_at column and a partial index let the worker poll due rows; rows past 24 h move to dead_letters.
shorts.picture: five boxes with table and column names

shorts.headline: Idempotency-Key header on every delivery
shorts.caption: Each delivery now carries the event id in an Idempotency-Key header.

shorts.headline: Every attempt shows in the event log
shorts.caption: The event log lists each attempt with its status code and delay.
shorts.why: Support can see why an event was late.

examples.why: A two-card story told in four shorts. The first opens on mechanism (backoff, jitter, 5xx) instead of the news a customer feels. hooks-queue is internals nobody would miss; hooks-key repeats the first short's idempotency point. Captions run past 30 words, and the first picture is too dense to read. The ms values are in the data but aren't the news.

thread.title: Failed webhooks now retry on their own

cards.headline: Retries show in the event log

shorts.headline: Failed webhooks now retry for up to a day
shorts.caption: When a customer's server is down, we keep trying instead of dropping the event.
shorts.why: Fewer missed events to chase by hand.
shorts.picture: three attempts on a timeline: two ✕ in the bad tone, the third ✓ delivered; four labels

examples.why: One short carries the story: what changed and who it helps, in 21 words, with a picture you read at a glance. The log card is a detail for the digest. Partner gets 4: it doesn't say that retried events may arrive twice.

examples.why: The second short earns its seconds: it is the change support will notice. Both stay short. It passes, though one short would have done.
